subject: Key lifecycle, TLS profile and HSM integration — Eastbridge RFP follow-up

Subject: Key lifecycle, TLS profile and HSM integration — Eastbridge RFP follow-up

Hi Michael,

Thanks for sharing Eastbridge's encryption questionnaire. Attached is our initial KMS/HSM response packet (Eastbridge_RFP_KMS_Answers_v1.pdf) — it covers high-level architecture, BYOK import options, rotation policies, and TLS/transit controls.

Top-line clarifications up front:
- We support envelope encryption across all deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Customer root keys can be BYOK (imported/wrapped) or resident in cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure).
- BYOK import uses secure, asymmetric-wrapped import tokens (no plaintext key material sent over email). For Private deployments we also support PKCS#11 and KMIP-backed HSMs.
- Key rotation: customer-controlled rotation schedules; recommended DEK rotation is 90 days for high-sensitivity workloads; master key rotation supported without forcing immediate re-encryption via new envelope keys.
- TLS: TLS 1.3 only on all public endpoints with ECDHE (X25519/P-256), AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305). mTLS is available for Dedicated and Private control-plane endpoints.

See the attachment for more detailed matrix and examples. Willing to hop on a 30-min technical call with your security team if you want deep-dive demos of the import flow and HSM attestations.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which KMS/HSM option you prefer (AWS KMS, BYOK via import, or on-prem KMIP HSM).
2) If BYOK, tell us whether you need asymmetric-wrapped import or direct PKCS#11 import (Private).
3) Schedule a security call — happy to include our Infosec and Product Security engineers.

Thanks,

Sergio — thanks for the packet, helpful. A few clarifications before we bring this to our procurement/security review: 

1) BYOK import: can you confirm the exact import mechanism and whether Redwood ever has access to the unwrapped root key during the import? We need a clear statement for our compliance team.

2) Rotation semantics: you mention preserving ciphertext on master key rotation. Can you outline the re-encryption strategy and any risk windows when old DEKs are retired?

3) HSM attestations: do you provide vendor attestation (FIPS 140-2/3, module IDs) for the HSMs you integrate with (e.g., Luna, CloudHSM)? We need a copy of latest attestation/report.

4) TLS specifics: our compliance requires confirmation of supported cipher suites and whether TLS 1.2 connections are allowed anywhere (they must be disabled).

If you can address those four items in writing, we can move to scheduling a short technical call. Also please include a suggested agenda for the call and which security engineers you'd bring.

Michael — thanks for the targeted questions. Below are explicit answers you can share with your compliance team. I've attached our concise HSM attestation summary (hsm_attestation_summary.pdf) and included a suggested agenda for a 30-min call.

1) BYOK import mechanism and plaintext exposure
- Import method: For cloud-hosted BYOK we use asymmetric-wrapped key import (RFC 8017 / RSA-OAEP style). The customer generates or provides a DEK/Master Key, wraps it with a Redwood-provided public import key, and uploads the wrapped blob via our secure import endpoint. For Private deployments we also support PKCS#11 and KMIP direct imports to customer-managed HSMs.
- Plaintext exposure: Redwood does NOT persist or log unwrapped key material. Unwrapping of a wrapped import blob occurs only inside the target HSM (or within the customer KMS for cloud-managed keys). For Hosted BYOK we offer a "zero-knowledge" import mode where unwrapping is performed ephemeral inside a short-lived HSM instance that is not retained by Redwood beyond the import transaction; audit logs capture the import event but not the key material.

2) Key rotation and re-encryption semantics
- Envelope model: We use an envelope encryption model where Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) encrypt application data and are themselves wrapped by a Master Key (KEK).
- Rotation strategy: When a Master Key (KEK) rotates, new DEKs are issued and wrapped with the new KEK. Existing ciphertext remains decryptable because the prior KEK material is retained for auditing and selective decrypt during the transition window. Customers control rotation windows; typical guidance: rotate DEKs every 90 days, rotate KEKs every 12 months unless compliance requires more frequent rotation.
- Re-encryption: We support both live re-encryption (background rewrap/re-encrypt of stored objects) and lazy re-encryption (objects re-encrypted on next write). Re-encryption is optional; customers may elect immediate re-encryption if required by policy. All rotation operations are logged and can be exported to your SIEM.

3) HSM attestations and vendor support
- Supported HSMs: AWS CloudHSM, Thales Luna (via Luna SA / Luna HSM integrations), and KMIP-compatible devices (e.g., Utimaco, Gemalto) for Private deployments.
- Attestation: Attached summary (hsm_attestation_summary.pdf) includes module IDs, FIPS 140-2/3 status (where applicable), typical expiration of attestation reports, and contact for scheduling a live attestation review. For Hosted environments we rely on cloud HSM provider attestations (CloudHSM and KMS).

4) TLS profile and cipher suites
- TLS baseline: TLS 1.3 only on all externally-facing endpoints. We have deprecated TLS 1.2 and it is disabled for API and data-plane traffic.
- Cipher suites: ECDHE key exchange with X25519 and P-256; AEAD ciphers prioritized: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256.
- mTLS: Available for Dedicated and Private control-plane and inter-service communication where requested.
- Additional controls: HSTS on web consoles, secure renegotiation disabled, session resumption via ticket encryption, and strict cipher policy enforced at the load balancer and service layer.

Suggested 30-min call agenda:
- 0-5m: Intros and scope (who needs access to attestation artifacts)
- 5-15m: BYOK import demo and PKCS#11/KMIP options (Product Security + Infra)
- 15-25m: HSM attestation details and timeline (Product Security)
- 25-30m: Next steps and artifact handoff (Doc upload / Docusign NDA if needed)

Attendees we will bring: Neha Kapoor (Director, Product Security), an infra engineer for PKCS#11 demo, and me for commercial/operational items.

Documents attached: hsm_attestation_summary.pdf (concise attestation and module list)

Please let me know a couple of time slots that work for your team this week and I'll set up the invite. Happy to add any additional artifacts you need.
